title: Haile Selassie Addresses the League of Nations
text:
In October 1935 Fascist Italy invaded Ethiopia, one of the few independent African states and a member of the League of Nations. The League condemned the invasion but imposed only limited sanctions, leaving out oil. The Italian forces used aircraft to spray mustard gas on soldiers and civilians. In May 1936 Addis Ababa fell, and Emperor Haile Selassie went into exile.

On June 30, 1936, he addressed the League's Assembly in Geneva. When he came to the rostrum, a group of Italian journalists in the gallery began whistling and shouting abuse, and they were removed.

Speaking in Amharic, the emperor described in detail how the gas had been sprayed from planes over the land, killing people and animals and poisoning the waters. He reminded the members of the promises of collective security in the League's covenant, on which his country had relied. What was at stake, he said, was not only Ethiopia, but collective security, the very existence of the League, and the value of promises made to small states. He asked what reply he should take back to his people.

Within days the League voted to lift its sanctions on Italy. Three years later Europe was at war. Haile Selassie returned to Addis Ababa in 1941.
lesson: Speaking the truth plainly in defeat can preserve your dignity and your cause, even when the powerful choose not to listen.
source: League of Nations, Official Journal, Records of the Assembly, 1936; text of Haile Selassie's speech
